newsitem.title: USA: US spot natgas regains strength, leads Aug higher.
newsitem.headline: US spot natgas regains strength, leads Aug higher.

text.p: U.S. spot gas prices edged two to three cents higher Tuesday as traders anticipated warmer temperatures for the first few days of August.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, physical prices rose an average of three to four cents to $2.21-2.24 per mmBtu at Henry Hub, with the bulk of the deals reported done around $2.22.
According to Weather Services Corp, temperatures throughout Texas and the southern plains are expected to remain slightly above normal through the weekend.
This forecast also kept south Texas prices firm at $2.16-2.18, with Katy quoted in the low-$2.20s.
In the Midwest, where above-normal temperatures are expected to arrive Saturday, prices gained about two cents to $2.10-2.13. Chicago city-gate was talked in the low-$2.30s.
Prices for August 1 delivery were also quoted a bit higher at $2.05-2.07.
In the Permian Basin market, prices for Wednesday delivery jumped two cents to about $2.14-2.16.
San Juan prices moved to about $2.10-2.12, while southern California border prices rose three cents to $2.26-2.28.
Near-normal temperatures are forecast to continue in the Southwest through week's end, WSC reported.
In the East, swing gas at the New York city gate remained strong in the low-$2.40s.
